description: This high-resolution false-colour satellite image, likely from a Spot 5 sensor using a Near-Infrared (NIR)/Red/Green band combination, displays a rugged mountainous or volcanic landscape. Dark grey areas represent extensive bare rock, block litter, scree, or volcanic terrain, consistent with Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) land cover categories like "6.3.1.2 Scree" or "6.3.1.1 Bare rocks formations." Reddish-brown areas indicate sparsely vegetated terrain, where vegetation appears red due to the NIR band, possibly meeting the "< 10% vegetation" criterion for scree. The image features thick cyan (light blue) lines delineating major land cover boundaries, enclosing a large dark grey area. Thinner, irregular yellow lines mark additional features or sub-boundaries within the reddish and dark grey terrains. The image serves as a visual example of complex exposed geological environments for land cover mapping.
